gen-dafont-nickname-fs-erode: Erode is a text serif with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, set under Nickname's cozy, hand-drawn lettering. Its dignity is the strongest card here.
gen-dafont-nickname-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads wide and generous, its curves opening at both ends and its tall x-height filling each line. Beside Nickname's closed, hand-drawn shapes it feels comfortable in small doses.
gen-dafont-nickname-fs-public-sans: Public Sans comes across as hefty and trustworthy, with broad open counters on its rounder letters. Nickname's handwritten warmth sits above it, and the two share the page without fighting over it.
gen-dafont-nickname-general-sans: General Sans fills the line with a tall x-height. Its pen pressure never wavers, so after Nickname's cozy handwriting a longer passage would feel smooth, though it was not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-dafont-nickname-manrope: Manrope has bright, open mouths on every curve. Nickname is best at relaxed, hand-drawn charm with closed shapes, while Manrope is best at a single-width line that suits short stretches of reading.
gen-dafont-nickname-satoshi: Soaring and open, Satoshi lifts its x-height high while Nickname stays cozy and hand-drawn up top. The strongest quality here is how relaxed the closed and open shapes feel.
gen-dafont-nickname-switzer: Wire-like and Swiss, Switzer holds its c tips well apart and stands tall at the waist beneath Nickname's cozy handwriting. Its strongest quality is approachable openness, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-dafont-nickname-work-sans: Modern and high-waisted, Work Sans keeps its c tips apart. Under Nickname's closed, hand-drawn heading, a longer passage would feel comfortable in small doses, with joins as thick as the strokes.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee reads friendly and neutral, its terminals finishing well clear of the stem and its mean line set high. Nordic does powerful, ancient, brush-dab spacing best, while ABeeZee does open, approachable text best.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-aldrich: Aldrich reads modern and professional, with an x-height close to the cap height and round letters that look cupped. And Nordic's ancient, brush-dab spacing above it makes a longer passage feel like tracing one thick thread.
